name: MM-OptBench
description: MM-OptBench is a solver-grounded benchmark for multimodal optimization modeling: 780 English-language test instances spanning six optimization families and 26 problem types. Each instance combines task text with one to four rendered visual inputs, with 939 input images in total. The dataset also supplies complete textual specifications, structured instance data, mathematical formulations, reference solvers, and reference solutions. The release is a fixed test set; it does not define training or validation splits.

citation.name: MM-OptBench: A Solver-Grounded Benchmark for Multimodal Optimization Modeling

rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark covers controlled, application-inspired rendered artifacts and small-to-moderate optimization instances. It does not establish generalization to naturally occurring, noisy, interactive, or industrial-scale inputs. Instance-level solution checks do not prove semantic equivalence of every generated formulation. Benchmark scores alone should not be used to approve autonomous decisions in operational or safety-critical settings.
rai:dataBiases: Selection reflects the authors' choice of six mathematical families, 26 problem types, English task wording, generator parameters, and visual templates. Balanced difficulty groups are a benchmark design choice rather than estimates of real deployment frequencies. Other languages, artifact styles, and optimization structures may be underrepresented.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The released instances are synthetic optimization problems, not records collected from people. They are not intended to contain personal or sensitive information about real individuals. Author names and affiliations in this metadata provide attribution.
rai:dataUseCases: The intended use is research evaluation of mapping task text and visual artifacts to optimization models, executable solver code, and feasible solutions. Aligned structured inputs and solver references support evaluation on the instantiated tasks and oracle-input comparisons. Construct validity for fairness assessment, demographic evaluation, and industrial deployment has not been established.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark may support more accessible and reliable optimization modeling tools. Misinterpreting benchmark performance as operational reliability could contribute to infeasible, unfair, unsafe, or costly decisions. The documented task scope and explicit feasibility/objective checks support careful interpretation; deployment still requires domain-specific validation and human oversight.
rai:dataCollection: Authors and research colleagues with optimization expertise defined problem families, generators, reference solvers, visual templates, and validation rules. Structured instances were generated, solved, rendered, and checked for visual and cross-modal consistency. The released metadata retains generation seeds under seed or random_seed; exact structured inputs are supplied in ground_truth/instance_data.json.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Reference mathematical models and solutions are paired with the generated structured instances. Solver checks and expert review cover visual readability, cross-modal consistency, and task constraints. Construction used no paid crowdsourcing.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors maintain the public GitHub repository. Users can report data or code issues through GitHub Issues. This Croissant file identifies an immutable dataset snapshot; later dataset changes should use a new version and updated metadata.

prov:wasDerivedFrom.name: Synthetic instance parameters and generation seeds
prov:wasDerivedFrom.description: Source parameters are preserved in each ground_truth/instance_data.json; generation seeds are recorded under seed or random_seed in the corresponding meta.json. These are synthetic sources, not an external collected dataset.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: Solver-grounded multimodal instance construction
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Optimization experts designed a taxonomy and parameterized generators. Candidate structured instances were solved and screened; aligned mathematical models, reference solutions, task text, and static visual artifacts were produced and checked for solver, visual, and cross-modal consistency. The retained release contains 780 test instances. Construction methodology is described in the paper and repository README.

prov:wasAssociatedWith.name: MM-OptBench authors and research colleagues with optimization expertise
